problems.reason: All three sentences state that Imperobator lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
Both sentences describe the fossils as belonging to the Cape Lamb Member of the Snow Hill Island Formation on James Ross Island.
Both sentences discuss the debate over whether Imperobator is a dromaeosaur and its size relative to other taxa.
Both sentences mention ongoing debate about the classification of Imperobator.

Sentences 21 and 22 state that the Paleobiology Database places Imperobator in Dromaeosauridae, while sentences 18, 19, and 20 describe it as a Paraves, basal deinonychosaur, or possible unenlagiine, which conflicts with the Dromaeosauridae assignment.
